questions.q: What is used to join Concrete pipes?
questions.n: Mortar is the traditional and standard bonding agent used to create secure joints between sections of concrete piping.

questions.q: A flexible type of pipe known for being the only plastic tubing suitable for use with hot or cold-water pressure systems?
questions.n: Polybutylene was specifically recognized for its flexibility and ability to handle both hot and cold pressurized water.

questions.q: What is the minimum size of the supply pipe distributing the main line to the primary branch?
questions.n: A 50 mm pipe provides the necessary volume and pressure capacity to serve as the primary distribution branch from the main.

questions.q: Which of the following practices is considered illegal?
o: Connecting a dishwasher to a food waste disposer
Using copper tubing for gas lines
Installing a check valve on the water heater inlet
Using a booster pump to draw water directly from the main line and distributing it to buildings
questions.n: Drawing directly from the main can cause a vacuum that collapses pipes or contaminates the public supply; a suction tank should be used instead.

questions.q: In a three-storey residential building, where is the water pressure the highest?
questions.n: Water pressure is highest at the lowest point of the system because of the weight of the water column above it.

questions.q: What type of valve is typically installed at the entry point of a water service line to control the entire building’s supply?
questions.n: Gate valves provide a full, unobstructed flow when open, making them ideal for the main isolation valve of a building.

questions.q: What is the greenish stain that forms on copper pipes or tubes over time?
questions.n: Patina is the green film formed on the surface of copper due to oxidation over a long period.

questions.q: What type of pipe is best used for grease traps?
questions.n: Stainless steel offers superior durability and resistance to corrosion and heat, which is essential for grease trap applications.

questions.q: Which type of pipe fitting should be used if you want to increase the water pressure?
questions.n: By narrowing the pipe diameter, a reducer increases the velocity and pressure of the water flow.

questions.q: Why don't water closets need a P-trap?
o: They connect to a vent stack directly
The water level is high enough
questions.n: Water closets are designed with an internal trapway that functions as a trap, making an external P-trap unnecessary.

questions.q: What hand tool is used to flare pipes?
questions.n: A flare tool is specifically engineered to spread the end of a soft metal tube into a funnel shape to create a leak-proof mechanical joint.

questions.q: Which valve provides fine and precise control of flow?
questions.n: Needle valves feature a slender, tapered point that allows for extremely incremental adjustments to the volume of fluid passing through.

questions.q: What tool is used to remove burrs from the inside of a cut pipe?
questions.n: A reamer is a rotary cutting tool designed to smooth out and enlarge the internal diameter of a pipe by removing sharp edges left after cutting.

questions.q: What valve is typically installed at the base of water tanks to prevent backflow?
questions.n: A foot valve is a type of check valve placed at the bottom of a suction line to keep the pump primed and prevent water from draining back into the source.

questions.q: This fitting changes the direction of a pipe at a 45-degree angle?
questions.n: An elbow fitting is named for the specific degree of the bend it provides in the piping run.

questions.q: This is a hardware component used to secure or hang pipes from a structure like a wall or ceiling?
questions.n: Pipe clamps or hangers provide the necessary structural support to keep pipes in place and prevent sagging or vibration.

questions.q: This is a standard bathroom fixture used for hanging towels?
questions.n: A towel rack is the designated wall-mounted fixture intended for the storage and drying of towels in a bathroom.

questions.q: This is a mixing valve used to control the flow and temperature specifically for a shower assembly?
questions.n: A shower valve manages both the volume of water and the ratio of hot-to-cold water delivered to the shower head.

questions.q: This allows fire department pumpers to supplement the building's fire protection system?
questions.n: A Siamese connection is an external inlet with two or more openings that allows fire engines to pump water into the building's fire system.

questions.q: which is the primary point for disposing of wastewater from floor surfaces?
questions.n: A floor drain is a fixture installed in a floor to collect and convey wastewater from the surrounding surface into the drainage system.

questions.q: the short section of pipe that connects the fixture outlet (like a sink) to the trap?
questions.n: The tailpiece is the specific tubular fitting that bridges the gap between the fixture's drain opening and the trap.

questions.q: washbasin, typically found in bathrooms?
questions.n: In plumbing terminology, a lavatory refers specifically to the washbasin used for personal hygiene in a bathroom.

questions.q: designed with deep basins for heavy-duty washing?
questions.n: Laundry tubs (or utility sinks) have deep basins specifically intended for soaking clothes or heavy rinsing.

questions.q: These are widely used in residential bathrooms to provide on-demand hot water without a central storage tank?
questions.n: Single point heaters (tankless) provide instantaneous hot water directly at the fixture where they are installed.

questions.q: is a specialized valve located at the property line, accessible via a curb box, allowing the water authority to shut off service.
questions.n: A curb stop is the control valve for the water service that is placed in the ground near the street curb for utility access.

questions.q: These systems use solar collectors to transfer heat from the sun to the water stored in the integrated tank?
questions.n: Solar water heaters utilize renewable energy from the sun to warm water through thermal collectors.

questions.q: When a valve closes quickly, the sudden stop of water flow creates a shockwave. This vertical "air chamber" or piston device absorbs that energy to prevent the "thumping" sound?
questions.n: An arrestor provides a cushion (usually air) to dissipate the shockwave energy known as 'water hammer' when valves close abruptly.

questions.q: As the water level rises, the buoyant ball lifts the arm, which mechanically closes the valve at a predetermined height?
questions.n: Float valves use buoyancy to automatically shut off the water supply once a tank or bowl reaches a certain fill level.

questions.q: What is a 180-degree bend in a pipe called?
questions.n: A return bend is a fitting that turns the flow of the pipe 180 degrees, directing it back toward the source.

questions.q: Which coupling device is used to connect two pipes that cannot be turned...?
questions.n: A union has a three-piece design that allows two stationary pipes to be joined without rotating the pipes themselves.

questions.q: Which type of fitting is used for a yoke vent?
questions.n: Wye fittings provide a smoother 45-degree branch connection, which is the standard for connecting a yoke vent between a soil stack and a vent stack.

questions.q: What part of the P-trap should the trap seal cover?
o: bottom of crown weir to top of dip
top of the pipe to the bottom of the pipe
crown weir to the floor drain
questions.n: The trap seal is the vertical distance between the top of the dip (the lowest point of the upper interior surface) and the crown weir (the lowest point of the discharge opening).

questions.q: Which plumbing fixture does NOT have a water-saving feature?
questions.n: A pop-up drain is a mechanical stopper and does not inherently regulate or reduce the volume of water used by the faucet.

questions.q: For a T&B (Toilet and Bath) on the ground floor, which should be connected directly under the floor drain?
questions.n: Every floor drain requires a P-trap immediately below it to maintain a water seal and prevent sewer gases from entering the room.

questions.q: What is the BEST fixture for a public comfort room?
questions.n: Flushometer valves provide high-pressure, instantaneous flushing and can be used repeatedly without waiting for a tank to refill.

questions.q: Which pipe fitting is used to join two straight lengths of pipe?
questions.n: A coupling is a short sleeve used to connect two pipes of the same diameter in a continuous straight run.

questions.q: What is the typical slope for a waste pipe?
questions.n: A 2% slope (approximately 1/4 inch per foot) is the industry standard to ensure water flows at the correct velocity to carry solids.

questions.q: Which fitting is threaded on the outside and used to connect pipes or fittings?
questions.n: A nipple is a short length of pipe with external (male) threads at both ends used for connecting other fittings.

questions.q: According to the NPC (National Plumbing Code), pipe supports should be placed every ?
questions.n: The 3-meter interval is a standard maximum distance between supports for horizontal piping to prevent sagging.

questions.q: T & S is the abbreviation for ?
questions.n: In architectural and plumbing plans, 'T & S' is used to denote a combination bathtub and shower unit.

questions.q: WC is the abbreviation for ?
questions.n: WC is the internationally recognized technical abbreviation for a toilet.

questions.q: FD is most commonly used as an abbreviation for ?
questions.n: FD is the standard plumbing abbreviation found on floor plans to indicate the location of a floor drain.

questions.q: A gooseneck spout is used on ?
questions.n: Gooseneck spouts are high-arching faucet designs commonly used on kitchen or laboratory sinks to provide clearance for large items.

questions.q: Which faucet is best used outside, especially in a garden?
questions.n: A hose bibb is a heavy-duty outdoor faucet with a threaded outlet specifically designed for attaching a garden hose.

questions.q: There are several reasons why soil stacks are not allowed in columns. Which of the following is NOT a reason?
o: It creates a void in the compression member
Repairs would require damaging the structure
The gas emitted will deteriorate the concrete
It reduces the structural strength of the column
questions.n: While sewer gas is unpleasant, the primary reasons for the ban are related to structural integrity and accessibility, not chemical deterioration of concrete.

questions.q: Which type of pipe conveys the discharge from water closets or similar fixtures?
questions.n: A soil pipe is the technical term for any pipe that carries discharge from toilets (water closets) or urinals containing human waste.

questions.q: Which of the following should NOT be placed in line with a beam?
questions.n: The large drain required for a water closet (usually 3 or 4 inches) would require cutting through the beam, which is structurally prohibited.

questions.q: Which material should be used for sanitary pipes?
questions.n: Unplasticized Polyvinyl Chloride (uPVC) is the most common material for sanitary drainage due to its corrosion resistance and smooth interior.

questions.q: What is the typical size of a pipe connected to sinks for its drain and trap arm?
questions.n: A 2-inch diameter is the standard minimum size for sink trap arms and waste lines to ensure adequate drainage.

questions.q: Excavated soil should not be placed any closer than ?
questions.n: Safety codes require excavated material to be kept at least 600 mm (about 2 feet) from the edge of the trench to prevent cave-ins.

questions.q: What is the minimum size of a floor drain cover?
questions.n: A 4-inch by 4-inch grate is the standard minimum size to provide sufficient drainage for a typical bathroom or utility floor.

questions.q: What do you call a panel placed in the wall to provide access to valves and fittings?
questions.n: Access panels are removable or hinged plates that allow maintenance of plumbing, electrical, or HVAC components hidden behind walls.

questions.q: What is the primary point for disposing of wastewater from floor surfaces?
questions.n: A floor drain is specifically designed to be the lowest point in a floor to collect water and direct it into the sanitary system.

questions.q: What is used to join Concrete pipes?
questions.n: Concrete pipes are joined using mortar to create a sealed, cement-based connection.

questions.q: A flexible type of pipe known for being the only plastic tubing suitable for use with hot or cold-water pressure systems?
questions.n: Polybutylene was widely marketed for its ability to handle temperature fluctuations in pressurized domestic water systems.

questions.q: What is the minimum size of the supply pipe distributing the main line to the primary branch?
questions.n: Standard plumbing regulations often specify a 50 mm minimum for primary distribution lines to ensure adequate flow velocity and pressure.

questions.q: Which of the following practices is considered illegal?
o: Venting a sink through a roof
Using PEX for hot water lines
Using a booster pump to draw water directly from the main line and distributing it to buildings
questions.n: Drawing water directly from the public main can cause negative pressure and collapse pipes or contaminate the supply; a cistern is required.

questions.q: In a three-storey residential building, where is the water pressure the highest?
questions.n: Pressure is highest at the lowest elevation because the water has the greatest amount of weight (head) pushing down on it.

questions.q: What type of valve is typically installed at the entry point of a water service line to control the entire building’s supply?
questions.n: Gate valves allow for full flow when open and provide a reliable shut-off for the main service entry.

questions.q: What is the greenish stain that forms on copper pipes or tubes over time?
questions.n: Patina is the natural oxidation layer that develops on copper, protecting the underlying metal while turning it green.
